title: POC Weekly Sync - Model Selection and Pinning - ACME Retail
summary: Weekly POC sync to review model comparison results, decide on model pinning for the pilot, discuss rollback/fallback strategy and next steps. Customer saw better cost/latency tradeoffs on a quantized 7B variant but prefers rw-instruct-13b for QA. Action items: Redwood to share updated benchmark spreadsheet, pricing with dedicated pilot options, and config for pinning/rollbacks; customer to run additional evals on edge-case prompts and confirm acceptance criteria.
topics: Model comparison (rw-instruct-13b vs rw-7b-quant vs openllama-13B)
header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Sam Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM); Jamal Carter (ACME - Lead ML Eng), Anika Patel (ACME - Product), Liam Ng (ACME - SRE), Rachel Yu (ACME - Data)
transcript:
[00:00] Sam Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have Priya from the SE team and Diego on the CSM side. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:12] Jamal Carter: Yep, all good here.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Great, thanks. Agenda for today: go over the benchmark spreadsheet you ran, talk model pinning options, fallback/rollback behaviour, and next steps for the pilot.
[00:33] Anika Patel: Sounds good. We got the spreadsheet, thanks. We have some questions on the latency numbers.
[00:40] Priya Singh: Cool, before we jump in quick reminder: we normally recommend pinning at the model-version level — e.g., rw-instruct-13b-v1.2 — and having a fallback chain to a smaller quantized variant if capacity or SLOs are breached.
[00:58] Liam Ng: Can you restate fallback behaviour? If p95 latency spikes do you automatically route to the fallback or queue?
[01:05] Priya Singh: You can do either. By default Redwood routing can be set to automatic fallback to a compatible variant based on policy (latency-first or cost-first). So if rw-instruct-13b-v1.2 is degraded beyond threshold, it falls back to rw-7b-quant-v1.0, which has lower cost but slightly lower factuality in our evals.
[01:28] Jamal Carter: That's helpful. Looking at the sheet we ran tests at 512 tokens. The p50/p95 for rw-instruct-13b-v1.2 is 210ms / 620ms, throughput ~18 tokens/sec. The quantized 7B had p50/p95 120ms / 340ms and about 35 tokens/sec.
[01:48] Priya Singh: Those numbers line up with what we expect on the Dedicated nodes we used for your pilot. Important note: the 13B was running the full fp16 path; if you want sub-200 p50 you generally need a different compilation profile or lower sequence length or use half-precision kernel selection.
[02:08] Rachel Yu: On quality, we ran 200 eval prompts and saw 4% hallucination rate on 13B and 7% on the 7B quant. But the 7B did better on short completion time-to-first-token.
[02:24] Sam Ortiz: Right, so it's very much a latency vs quality tradeoff. For the pilot success criteria, have we agreed numeric thresholds?
[02:33] Anika Patel: We said p95 under 700ms for key flows, and accuracy above 92% on our acceptance set.
[02:40] Jamal Carter: We might tweak acceptance to allow 90% if latency improvements are significant.
[02:46] Priya Singh: Ok, that gives us a little wiggle room. On pinning — two practical approaches: 1) pin to rw-instruct-13b-v1.2 for all prod routes, and configure automatic fallback to rw-7b-quant-v1.0 when latency SLO is broken; 2) use A/B pinning where 80% goes to 13B and 20% to 7B-quant to measure drift in production and costs.
[03:10] Liam Ng: For SRE we prefer automatic fallback with logging/tracing for each switch so we can audit behavior. Is that implemented?
[03:18] Priya Singh: Yes — the Redwood Console exposes per-request trace headers and you can tag fallbacks. We also emit audit events to your Kinesis/S3 (or your SIEM) depending on integration; for private deployments we can push to your VPC endpoints and use your KMS for envelope encryption.
[03:34] Jamal Carter: Security question — does fallback switching leak any request data to the fallback model or external systems?
[03:40] Sam Ortiz: No, it's internal to the runtime. All models in your private catalog run in your tenancy/fleet, the request payload stays within the customer-controlled environment. If using hosted with dedicated tenancy we still keep isolation but we'd want to confirm data retention and retention windows. We'll share the security doc.
[03:58] Anika Patel: Great. Back to the model list: in addition to the two variants, we ran openllama-13b-v0.9 as a baseline and it had similar quality but higher latency — p95 was closer to 780ms. So it's not ideal.
[04:14] Priya Singh: Thanks for running that. The choice seems between consistent higher-quality 13B or faster/cheaper 7B-quant. For the pilot it's common to pin to the higher quality variant and enable automatic fallback for bursty traffic to reduce user-visible latency.
[04:30] Rachel Yu: One odd thing in the spreadsheet — there were a couple of prompts where the 13B returned truncated code blocks more often; could that be a sampling or tokenizer mismatch?
[04:40] Priya Singh: Potentially. We sometimes see corpus tokenization edge-cases between tokenizers; we can run an alignment check. Also check generation settings — temperature/top_p and stop tokens. If you're using streaming vs non-streaming that changes behaviour too.
[04:58] Jamal Carter: On the operational front, how do we rollback a pinned version if we deploy v1.3 and see regressions?
[05:05] Priya Singh: There are two layers: immediate rollback — pin the route back to previous version (v1.2) which is an API call or Console click; automated rollback — you can configure a canary policy with health metrics (error rate, latency, perplexity on eval set) and automatic revert if it crosses thresholds for N minutes.
[05:24] Sam Ortiz: We recommend a canary for major model upgrades. For minor patch versions we often do a quick A/B plus manual verification.
[05:31] Anika Patel: For the A/B, can we route by endpoint only or by user segment?
[05:36] Priya Singh: Both — routing rules support headers, cookie, user id hash, or explicit segments from your identity provider.
[05:42] Liam Ng: What's the cost delta you're seeing in the sheet between the 13B and 7B-quant per 1k tokens?
[05:48] Sam Ortiz: Rough numbers from your runs: 13B on Dedicated ~ $0.48 per 1k tokens (hosted pricing varies), 7B-quant ~ $0.18 per 1k tokens. Those are ballpark and depend on batch size/cache hit rate. We'll include more exact numbers in the updated sheet.
[06:05] Jamal Carter: One operational ask: can we have a pinned route that prefers 13B but warms kv-cache on 7B-quant to speed fallback?
[06:14] Priya Singh: Cache warmup across model families is tricky because tokenization and hidden state shapes differ. However you can do prefix caching for common prompts and replicate cached KV states across variants that share architecture. We'll need to check compatibility between rw-instruct-13b and the quant variant — sometimes minor.
[06:33] Rachel Yu: Ok. For acceptance testing, we planned a 10k request soak over the next two weeks. Should we switch to the 7B-quant for a portion to reduce cost?
[06:44] Sam Ortiz: If you want to run a long soak, moving 30-50% to the 7B-quant is common to limit cost while retaining quality signals. Or use replay with synthetic traffic.
[06:55] Anika Patel: Let's talk timeline: we'd like to pin to 13B for user-facing flows by next Tuesday if metrics hold. Is that feasible?
[07:03] Priya Singh: Yes from Redwood side — we'll prepare pin config and can schedule a canary rollout. We just need your sign-off on the final acceptance set and the canary thresholds.
[07:12] Jamal Carter: We'll finish the extra 500 edge-case prompts today and upload results by EOD tomorrow.
[07:18] Sam Ortiz: Great. We'll also add an automated gating check we can run post-deploy to measure perplexity and a set of regression prompts.
[07:26] Diego Ramos: From the CSM perspective we'll set up weekly alerting and a shared Slack channel for rapid rollback if something odd happens.
[07:34] Liam Ng: One more question — for private deployment, are there any additional steps to pin versions?
[07:39] Priya Singh: No, same API and Console. For private we give you the private catalog UI and infra hooks. The difference is we don't touch your KMS keys or logs unless you opt-in to the support flow.
[07:50] Anika Patel: Anything else on compliance? SOC 2 docs?
[07:54] Sam Ortiz: We'll send the SOC 2 + ISO certs and our security whitepaper. Also include KMS integration guide.
[07:59] Jamal Carter: Ok sounds good.
[08:02] Priya Singh: Quick recap of agreements: continue with rw-instruct-13b-v1.2 as primary, enable automatic fallback to rw-7b-quant-v1.0 with tagged traces, run A/B for soak with 30-50% to 7B-quant, finish edge-case evals, Redwood to share updated benchmark and pricing, and prepare canary pin config.
[08:23] Anika Patel: Perfect.
[08:25] Sam Ortiz: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts.
[08:28] Jamal Carter: Thanks all.
[08:30] Meeting ends.

Notes: Transcript includes some mumbled words and a few misattributed speaker tags in short sections where recording overlapped. References in the call: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood-sharing/acme/pilot-benchmarks-2026-07-21), security packet (link: https://redwood-sharing/security/soc2), pinning config doc (link: https://redwood-sharing/docs/pinning).
